clue.text: Derisive remark from swine with clothing accessory

parts.note: a sow is a female pig
a hat is something worn to finish an outfit

explanation.surface: A sneer aimed at a pig dressed up in a fashion accessory.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is a dismissive retort showing the speaker does not care at all.

clue.text: Love hired clothing I adjusted

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring, which looks like the letter O

indicators.note: the hired word wraps round the single letter like a garment

parts.note: something hired has been rented
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tweaks the outfit they rented for a sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: To be oriented is to be aligned or positioned in a set direction, a synonym of adjusted.

clue.text: Swallowing tablet, experienced long migraine?

indicators.note: the word for experienced takes the tablet inside it, as if gulping it down

parts.note: to have had something is to have experienced it
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet
to ache for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: Someone takes a pill after suffering a lengthy migraine.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition by example: a migraine is one severe kind of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A migraine is a particularly severe example of a pain in the head.

clue.text: Theodore, catching babble, gossiped and giggled

indicators.note: the short name surrounds the word for babble, as though grabbing it

parts.note: Ted is a short form of the name Theodore
to witter is British slang for chattering on aimlessly

explanation.surface: A man called Theodore overhears some nonsense and spreads it around with a laugh.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds twitter, and by extension people who twitter chatter lightly and titter.

clue.text: Double dose of silly tosh for virtuosi

indicators.note: two helpings of the word, each made silly, i.e. jumbled up nonsensically

parts.note: the word is taken twice over, as the double dose demands

explanation.surface: Talented performers are fed twice the usual helping of rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Each copy of the four letters is rearranged the same way, giving a four-letter word twice. Tosh is British slang for nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Hotshots are people exceptionally skilled at something, just as virtuosi are masters of their art.

clue.text: At work, Rihanna must aim to maintain current, kindly attitude

indicators.note: the jumbled letters hold the symbol for current within them
the words are put to work, i.e. busily reorganised

parts.note: taken as written
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: The pop star Rihanna is urged to keep up a generous outlook while working.
explanation.definitionFit: Humanitarianism is the outlook of promoting human welfare, a benevolent view of others.

clue.text: Curse hideous courgette wraps

indicators.note: the two words enclose the answer within their letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook complains about an ugly vegetable dish wrapped up in pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: A scourge is a cause of great suffering, an affliction like a curse.

clue.text: Musical work, oddly trendy, worked in the theatre?

parts.note: an opera is a dramatic work set to music

indicators.note: only the letters in odd positions of the next word are used

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A modish musical production is described as having played in a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The theatre is not the stage but the operating theatre, where a surgeon works.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon who operated did surgery, i.e. worked in an operating theatre.

clue.text: Head of school blinking upset by 21 Across curriculum

indicators.note: the first letter of school is taken

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down so it reads backwards

parts.note: bally is a mild British euphemism for bloody, like blinking
the answer to 21 Across is AMERICAN, abbreviated as US

explanation.surface: A headteacher is annoyed by a blasted American course of study.
explanation.definitionFit: A syllabus is the outline of subjects in a course of study, as is a curriculum.

clue.text: Metal ship that went down, almost? I'm not sure

indicators.note: the ship's name is not quite complete, losing its last letter

parts.note: the Titanic famously sank in 1912
um is the hesitant sound of someone unsure

explanation.surface: Someone hesitantly wonders if a famous sinking ship was made of metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Titanium is a strong, light metallic element used in aircraft.

clue.text: Prosper in Germany? Need to repay £50

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany
to owe is to be required to pay back
the pound sign comes from L for the Latin libra
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Someone thriving in Germany still has fifty pounds to pay back.
explanation.definitionFit: To do well is to succeed or thrive, an idiom matching prosper.

clue.text: Curiously, ten fans following United take ties off

indicators.note: the jumbled letters come after the abbreviation

parts.note: U is a common abbreviation for United in team names

indicators.note: the words are arranged in a strange new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Ten football supporters trailing behind United strangely remove their scarves or neckties.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfasten is to undo or loosen bindings, i.e. to release what is tied.

clue.text: Mistakes from a sailor, about to head west

indicators.note: in an across clue, heading west means reading right to left

parts.note: taken as written
a tar is an old nickname for a sailor
re means regarding or about

explanation.surface: A seaman's errors concern his plan to sail westward.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata is the Latin plural for errors, used of misprints listed in a book.

clue.text: Legacy, or what not to ask a lady about it

indicators.note: the phrase goes round the little word

parts.words: what not to ask a lady
parts.note: etiquette holds you should never ask a woman her age
taken as written

explanation.surface: An inheritance, or a reminder of old-fashioned etiquette about asking women questions.
explanation.definitionFit: Heritage is what is handed down from earlier generations, an inheritance.

clue.text: Penny after old coin, as well as one grand for testee

indicators.note: the penny comes after the old coin

parts.note: a guinea was a British gold coin worth 21 shillings
I is the Roman numeral for one
G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: Money totted up: a penny, an old coin and a thousand.
explanation.definitionFit: A guinea pig is someone used as the subject of an experiment, i.e. one being tested.

clue.text: Outspoken star disinclined to work

indicators.note: the clue's word is to be heard spoken out, its sound giving the answer

parts.note: an idol is a celebrity who is adored

explanation.surface: A celebrity who speaks freely turns out to be lazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle means lazy, avoiding effort or activity.

clue.text: Chilled pumpkin for Malcolm? Only a portion of it

indicators.note: just a slice of the words' letters is wanted, like a portion of the pumpkin

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A chilled pumpkin is given to Malcolm, but he gets only a slice.
explanation.walkthrough: Chilled looks like a temperature but means relaxed, as in chilled out.
explanation.definitionFit: Chilled in slang means laid-back and relaxed, as is an informal occasion.

clue.text: What dissatisfied saver perhaps did somewhere in Paris

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an unhappy customer quit their bank
second meaning: the south bank of the Seine in Paris, known for artists

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is read once as a verb plus noun, once as a Parisian district's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rive Gauche, the artistic district south of the Seine, is called this in English.

clue.text: Father's moving daughter back, getting tots up

indicators.note: the letters shift position, with the daughter's D moved back one place

parts.note: dad's is the possessive of an informal name for father

explanation.surface: A dad is relocating his daughter while he totals up figures.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first D moves, one place back; daughter is D in crossword abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: To tot up is to sum figures, which is what one who adds does.

clue.text: Shiny silver rubbish thrown on the ground

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
litter is waste discarded in public places

explanation.surface: Bright silver junk scattered across the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Aglitter means glittering, sparkling with light.

clue.text: Excited in date with extremely excitable convict

indicators.note: the letters are stirred up into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: only the very ends of the next word are used

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A thrilled, highly strung prisoner is out on a date.
explanation.definitionFit: A detainee is someone held in custody, like a convict in prison.

clue.text: Loving installing last bit of garden decking

indicators.note: the loving word has the letter set inside it

parts.note: adoring means loving deeply

indicators.note: only the final letter of garden is used

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone happily putting in timber decking at the end of a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Decking looks like the timber platform in the garden, but it is the verb meaning decorating.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck is to decorate, so decking and adorning both mean embellishing.

clue.text: Group of people with high-flying jobs?

definitions.meaning: a team or crew of workers
seems to mean prestigious careers, but literally means work done up in the air

explanation.walkthrough: High-flying suggests ambitious executives; here it means literally flying high, as pilots and cabin staff do.
explanation.definitionFit: The aircrew is the team who staff an aeroplane in flight, working high above the ground.

clue.text: Unfashionable Conservative line generates protest

parts.note: something out is no longer in fashion
RY is short for railway, a rail line

explanation.surface: A dated Tory policy stirs up public objection.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcry is a loud public expression of disapproval, a strong protest.

clue.text: Maybe Morecambe toured by a chap from another country

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the name is gone round by the other letters

parts.note: a man is a chap
Eric Morecambe was a British comedian, so Morecambe suggests the name Eric

explanation.surface: A visitor from abroad travels round the English seaside town of Morecambe.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe looks like the Lancashire resort but stands for Eric Morecambe, half of the comedy duo Morecambe and Wise.
explanation.definitionFit: For a British setter, an American is someone or something from a foreign nation, the USA.

clue.text: Scanty dancing gear grabbed by yours truly

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are held inside the word for the setter

parts.note: the setter referring to themself, i.e. me

indicators.note: the letters jig about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The setter snatches some skimpy dancewear.
explanation.definitionFit: Meagre means lacking in quantity, small and insufficient.

clue.text: Ineffective mischief-maker with energy in both parts of the Bible

parts.note: an imp is a small mischievous sprite

indicators.note: the energy symbol sits between the two testaments

parts.note: the Old and New Testaments, abbreviated OT and NT

explanation.surface: A troublemaker brings vigour to scripture but achieves nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Impotent means lacking power or force, so unable to take effect.

clue.text: Rather cool enemy of Darth Vader with weapon

parts.note: Luke Skywalker fights Darth Vader in Star Wars
an arm is a weapon, as in firearms

explanation.surface: A Star Wars hero gets his weapon and is pretty unflappable.
explanation.walkthrough: Cool here means slightly chilly, not stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: Lukewarm means only moderately warm, tepid, neither hot nor cold.

clue.text: Presidents Washington and Bush, say, wanting English pigs out

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: George Washington and George Bush both share the first name George

explanation.surface: Two American presidents want English pigs expelled.
explanation.walkthrough: Pigs looks like animals in the surface, but pigs out is a phrasal verb for overeating.
explanation.definitionFit: To gorge is to stuff oneself greedily with food, eating like a glutton.
